profile.behavior: Walks over exposed flats and shallow shorelines, probing soft mud or wet sand and picking invertebrates and small crabs from the surface; often gathers in flocks outside the breeding season.
field_marks: Long, dark bill with a strong downward curve and subtle kink
Dark crown stripes divided by a pale central stripe, with a pale eyebrow
Dark eye crossed by a narrow dark eye-line
Gray-brown upperparts with pale-edged, scalloped feather patterning
Paler buff-gray underparts marked with fine dark streaks
Long gray legs, long pointed wings, and a short finely barred tail
profile.habitat: Breeds on open tundra, moorland, and low wet grassland; during migration and the nonbreeding season uses mudflats, sandy beaches, rocky shores, saltmarshes, estuaries, and other coastal wetlands.

findings: The primary specimen is a convincing Eurasian Whimbrel: one head and eye, one complete closed bill, a naturally occluded far-side wing, two plausibly attached legs with intact feet, and one short barred tail.

The bill in both depicted heads has the correct direction and degree of decurvature, including a straighter proximal section and stronger distal curve. Both mandibles trace continuously from a shared base to a coherent tip, with consistent proportions between the primary specimen and supplementary head study.

The plumage agrees with the references and direct-source descriptions: striped dark crown with pale median stripe, pale supercilium, narrow dark eyeline, gray-brown pale-edged upperparts, and finely streaked paler underparts.

The folded wing is long and pointed, the tail is short and barred, and the long gray legs and shorebird feet are anatomically credible. The detached spread-wing and head studies are clearly supplementary, independently plausible, and do not appear attached to the primary specimen.
All visible identification text is correct and complete: “Eurasian Whimbrel,” “Numenius phaeopus,” and “Scolopacidae.”
All three measurement lines exactly match the proposed and published values: “Length: 37–47 cm (15–19 in),” “Wingspan: 75–90 cm (30–35 in),” and “Weight: 270–493 g (9.5–17.4 oz).”
The habitat and behavior paragraphs reproduce the proposed wording without visible omissions, duplicated words, substitutions, misspellings, or numerical errors.
Every field-mark callout reproduces the proposed wording accurately and points to a corresponding visible feature.

The body-length diagram is internally consistent: 37 cm (15 in) is the lower endpoint, 47 cm (19 in) is the upper endpoint, values increase from bottom to top, and “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” clearly prevents interpreting it as the printed specimen’s scale.
The plate is clean, legible, balanced, and location-free; it contains no place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail.
